title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits among typed pages from a Bourbaki-style draft on jets (n° 382), but its handwritten content is unrelated: it is a sketch of crystalline deformation theory for Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups that carry an action of a ring A.

Setting, as far as it can be read:
- k is a perfect field of characteristic p and W = W(k).
- A is a finite extension of W, for example the ring of integers of a p-adic field, with uniformizer π. A is used both as the ring of coefficients acting on the group and as the base over which one lifts. The diagram Z_p → W → A, and the tensor products A⊗_{Z_p}W and A⊗_{Z_p}A, encode this double role.
- G_0 is a Barsotti–Tate group over k with an A-action. Its Dieudonné module is written M = Ω⊗_{Z_p}W, where Ω is the 'Z_p-structure', an A-module.
- Its value on A is M_A = Ω⊗_{Z_p}A.

Argument:
1. The page opens by concluding that 'such a lift exists and is unique (up to unique isomorphism)'.
2. To reduce to deformation theory, assume πA carries divided powers. Then A → k is a PD-thickening, and by Grothendieck(–Messing) crystalline deformation theory, lifting G_0 to G over A amounts to lifting the Hodge filtration of M⊗_W k = M_A⊗_A k to a direct-summand filtration of M_A.
3. Lifting compatibly with the A-action means the filtration must be stable under A⊗_{Z_p}A. Here one factor is the action of A on the group and the other is the base ring.
4. The Hodge sequence is 0 → ω_G → Ω⊗_{Z_p}A → t_{G*} → 0. By transposition one gets (**) 0 → ω_{G*} → Ω̌⊗_{Z_p}A → t_G → 0.
5. With the multiplication map p_0 : A⊗_{Z_p}A → A, p_0(λ⊗μ) = λμ, the hypothesis is that A acts on ω_G (equivalently on t_G) through its natural structure as an A-module. In other words, the two A-actions agree on the Lie algebra: G is a strict A-module.
6. This condition forces the filtration. The quotient must be the A-module obtained from A⊗A via p_0, so the submodule is determined by the kernel of p_0 (when Ω is free of rank one over A).
7. Hence a lift exists and is unique: this is the crystalline proof of existence and uniqueness of the canonical (Lubin–Tate–type) lift of a formal A-module, i.e. that a strict A-module of A-height one over k lifts uniquely to A.

So the page serves to show, by Dieudonné-crystal methods, that 'strict' A-actions rigidify deformations.
errors: The divided-power hypothesis on πA only holds for ramification e ≤ p−1, so the argument as written covers only mildly ramified A. Later Faltings/Zink/Lau methods for strict O-modules remove this restriction.

The role of Ω, and the claim that Ω⊗A is a rank-one A⊗A-module with the kernel of p_0 as the forced filtration, is only sketched. Freeness of Ω over A, i.e. A-height one, is implicitly needed for uniqueness.
The orientation of the Hodge sequence (ω_G as sub versus t_G as quotient) and the passage to the dual via (**) are stated loosely, with crossed-out attempts.

ideas.what: Lifting a BT group over a PD-thickening is equivalent to lifting the Hodge filtration of its Dieudonné crystal
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux (ICM Nice 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal, 1974)

ideas.what: Deformations with an A-action correspond to A⊗_{Z_p}A-stable filtrations; the condition that A acts naturally on Lie G pins the filtration down via the multiplication map p_0
ideas.modern_name: Strict formal O-modules / Kottwitz-type determinant (strictness) condition; crystalline construction of the canonical Lubin–Tate lift
ideas.where_published: possibly touched on in the Montréal lectures; unsure

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck formulates the strictness condition (A acts on ω_G / Lie G through the structure map) in crystalline terms, via the multiplication map A⊗_{Z_p}A → A. He uses it to get unique lifts of BT groups with A-action, anticipating the formal-O-module viewpoint of Drinfeld and the Lie-algebra conditions later standard in Rapoport–Zink theory.
missed.quote: L'hypothèse que A (où agit sur G) on l'action de A ... naturelle, signifie que ... ω_G ... provient de Ω ... p_0 : A⊗_{Z_p}A → A, p_0(λ⊗μ)=λμ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority detail: an early crystalline treatment of strict O-actions and canonical lifts. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early, unpublished sketch of the crystalline treatment of BT groups with strict A-action and their unique lifts. It is of historical interest as a precursor to the formal-O-module and Kottwitz-condition framework, but the mathematics is now standard and limited to e ≤ p−1.
transcription_corrections: 'πA est πΩ [?] puissance divisée' should likely read 'πA est muni de puissances divisées'.
'type de B.T.' should likely be 'groupe de B.T.'.
'sous-module direct 1 sur 1⊗A' is probably 'sous-module facteur direct, ... sur 1⊗A'.
In the bottom-left diagram the base is Z_p (it is written like 'Ψ_p'/'Z_p').
The phrase near 'sur ω_G' concerns the condition that the action of A on ω_G is the natural A-module structure, i.e. the module deduced by restriction of scalars via p_0.
